hook: SCP-966 is a short creature report built on a premise that sticks: something you cannot see takes away your ability to sleep, then waits. Look at the image caption and the camera requirements in the containment section first, since they quietly explain how anyone knows what these things look like. It takes a few minutes to read and works best as an idea that keeps unfolding after you finish.
whyItMatters: It is a tidy example of the predatory-species entry: a population loose in the world, task forces scanning the news for signs, and a handful of captured specimens in a lead-lined room. The danger is not claws or venom but an ordinary bodily need being switched off, which makes the threat feel quiet until you think it through. Pairing a body visible only through an infrared filter with a harm nobody can see at all is the core of its design.
thingsToNotice: The hunt is spelled out plainly: one burst of the unnamed wave permanently ends the victim's sleep, the creatures follow it silently, and once exhaustion drops it they eat it. They also make menacing sounds to raise the prey's stress and will attack outright if someone holds out too long. Some victims get repeated doses and suffer vivid hallucinations and sudden rage, and the report can only guess that hunger drives this. The physical description undercuts the monster on purpose, with hollow bones, brittle claws and weak muscles, because the prey wears itself down. Note too the cold line about the female: any offspring are to be studied and destroyed before adulthood, and the closing sentence admits large numbers are still loose in several countries.
